This is a repeat (fifth) application under Section 430 of the Bhartiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 for temporary suspension of jail sentence filed on behalf of appellant No.4 - Dashrath Singh Rathore S/o Mansingh Ji Rathore.
Counsel for the appellant submits that aforesaid I.A. has rendered infructuous as appellant No.4 has filed I.A. No.15618/2025 for regular suspension of jail sentence.
In view of the aforesaid, I.A. No.14978/2025 stands dismissed having been rendered infructuous.

This is a repeat (sixth) application under Section 430 of the Bhartiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita,
2023 for suspension of jail sentence and grant of bail filed on behalf of appellant No.4 - Dashrath Singh Rathore S/o Mansingh Ji Rathore.

This is a repeat (fourth) application under Section 430 of the Bhartiya 2 CRA-554-2024 Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 for suspension of jail sentence and grant of bail filed on behalf of appellant No.1 - Tej Singh S/o Dulesingh Ji Rajput.

Appellant No.4 suffered conviction and sentence as under:-

As per prosecution story, on 10.05.2021, mother of the prosecutrix lodged a report at Police Station - Banganga stating that her daughter went on a two-wheeler for bringing gas cylinder and did not return back, thereafter, a missing report was filed and FIR was registered.
During the investigation, the prosecutrix was recovered from the possession of co- accused - Dashrath Singh Rathore.

Thereafter, the police has recorded the statement of prosecutrix,
in which she revealed that on 07.05.2021, co- accused - Rajiya and Rajendra Singh took her to the house of sister of Rajendra naemly Santosh Kunwar, then co-accused - Santosh and Kailash called co-accused - Dashrath and arranged a meeting for her and Dashrath.
Thereafter, the marriage was fixed and solemnized on 14.05.2021.
Both of them travelled at different places as husband and wife and recovered by the police on 12.06.2021.
Counsel for the appellants argued that co-convicts - Santosh Kunwar and Kailash have already been given the benefit of suspension of jail sentence.
He argued that so far as case of appellant No.1 - Tej Singh is concerned, his case is almost on similar footing.

In regard to the allegation against appellant No.4, he said that from the statement of prosecutrix, it is manifest that the age of the prosecutrix was never disclosed to Dashrath who had married the prosecutrix.

He further argued that the moment appellant No.4 - Dashrath came to know the age of the prosecutrix,
he himself reported the matter to the police.
These appellants have undergone actual jail sentence of four years.
This is an appeal of 2024 and final hearing of the same is likely to take time.

Hence,
remaining jail sentence of these appellants be suspended.
Counsel for the State has opposed the application by submitting that earlier application of appellant No.4 has already been rejected on merit and there is no change in the circumstances.

In regard to appellant No.1, he has pointed out that in the video, appellant No.1 - Tej Singh is being seen taking the money, therefore, his case is different from the case of other co-convicts namely Santosh and Kailash.

After hearing learned counsel for the parties and considering the entire facts and evidence of the case, we find that appellant No.4 - Dashrath was not aware about the age of the prosecutrix and when he came to know about the age of the prosecutrix, he himself had reported the police.
We find that the prosecutrix was a consenting party in the present case, got married with appellant No.4 and stayed for about 1  months without raising any alarm at 4 CRA-554-2024 any point of time.

These appellants have already undergone four years of actual sentence and final hearing of this appeal may take time, therefore, we deem it expedient to suspend the remaining jail sentence of the these appellants.
Accordingly, I.A. Nos.15618/2025 & 1582/2026 stand allowed.

The execution of remaining jail sentence of appellant No.1 & 4 - Tej Singh & Dashrath Singh Rathore respectively shall remain suspended during the pendency of the appeal and they be released on bail upon their furnishing personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand Only) each Tejsingh vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 5 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/150286517/
2 with separate surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court and on depositing the fine amount (if not already deposited) with a further direction to appear before the Registry of this Court on 14.05.2026 , and thereafter, on all subsequent dates as may be fixed by the Registry in this regard during the pendency of the appeal.
